I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so at the start of the season I will keep to the cropping pattern that is most reliable for me: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That fits my land, water conditions, machinery, and the local climate better than trying something riskier. I have a middle level of schooling, so I will choose a management plan that is practical and familiar rather than complicated. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most of the phosphorus and potassium in as base fertilizer, split nitrogen between base and topdressing, irrigate at the key stages, and keep field work simple with rotary tillage. After wheat harvest, I will go straight into summer maize with hybrid seed because maize responds well and gives me stable yield. I will keep fertilizer moderate, watch weeds and insects, irrigate only when needed because summer rain helps, and aim for steady output instead of chasing the maximum. My main decision is to protect yield and control cost with the wheat-maize double-cropping system.
